about: The Act shelf (STATUTE_COVERAGE_PLAN.md step 2): Acts whose full text is loaded from India Code by build_act_chunks.py, checked against India Code's own PDF. 'corrections' are exact replacements of slips in India Code's database, each shown to be what the PDF reads; 'accepted' are spelling variants that are not slips. Nothing here says the text has been read by a person.

pointers.why: Section 8 makes GIVING an undue advantage to a public servant an offence; its provisos exempt a person who was compelled to give it only if he reports the matter to the law enforcement authority or investigating agency within seven days of giving it. A question in which the person paid or was made to pay never uses the words 'section 8', and a search by meaning ranks the offence of TAKING (s.7) first (staging 2026-10-17: the tehsildar answer said nothing about the payer's own position).

corrections.from:
[66A. Punishment for sending offensive messages through communication service, etc.--Any person who sends, by means of a computer resource or a communication device,
(a) any information that is grossly offensive or has menacing character; or
(b) any information which he knows to be false, but for the purpose of causing annoyance, inconvenience, danger, obstruction, insult, injury, criminal intimidation, enmity, hatred or ill will, persistently by making use of such computer resource or a communication device;
(c) any electronic mail or electronic mail message for the purpose of causing annoyance or inconvenience or to deceive or to mislead the addressee or recipient about the origin of such messages,
shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine.
Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, terms "electronic mail" and "electronic mail message" means a message or information created or transmitted or received on a computer, computer system, computer resource or communication device including attachments in text, image, audio, video and any other electronic record, which may be transmitted with the message.]
corrections.to: [Punishment for sending offensive messages through communication service, etc.]-- Omitted by the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 (18 of 2023), s. 2 and Schedule (w.e.f. 30-11-2023).
corrections.why: SUBSTANTIVE. India Code's database keeps the whole text of section 66A, which the Supreme Court struck down on 24 March 2015 (Shreya Singhal v. Section 132, the driver's duty to stop, is left to the search by meaning.
